brief: This is the third in a week-long CoTD series on the current Fed hiking cycle, the 15th in 70 years. Earlier notes found 10yr yields rose in the first year of 11 of the last 12 hiking cycles, and that market pricing implies this would be the shallowest hiking cycle in history. Today's chart plots CPI at the first hike against first-year tightening across the prior 14 cycles and finds a tight correlation: higher starting CPI means more first-year hiking. The six shallowest first-year cycles all began with CPI at or below 2%, and cycles with under 100bps of first-year tightening started with CPI near 1%. Applying the best-fit line to DB's 3.55% CPI forecast for this month implies just over 200bps of first-year hikes in the current cycle, an outcome nobody currently expects. But in 2022 nobody expected the eventual 400bps-plus either, when markets were pricing only 200bps at the time, so the note reads this as evidence markets tend to underestimate hiking-cycle scale early on.
